coachingPoints: Sprint the cut — screens only work at full speed; jogging through them gets you nothing.
Read the defender over your shoulder as you come off: trail, go over, or switch.
Keep your path tight — shoulder-to-shoulder with the screener, never looping wide.
Feet ready on the catch: hop into the shot or land ready to drive in one motion.
Practice both sides and both directions (curl, flare, straight) — game screens come in all shapes.
commonMistakes: Slowing down before the screen — fix: accelerate into the screen; speed creates the separation.
Running too wide around the screener — fix: brush shoulders with the screener; every extra foot is a recovered defender.
Catching flat-footed — fix: arrive in your shot-prep hop so you can shoot or drive instantly.
Only practicing uncontested — fix: add a chasing defender to reps so reads become instinct.
description: Sprint off screens, read the defender, and shoot in motion — the specialist skill of elite movement shooters.
gameSituations: Floppy and pin-down actions — sprint off the screen for a catch-and-shoot three while the defense chases.
Hammer and wide pin-downs — cross-court screens for corner threes in late-clock offense.
Against switching defenses — a tight curl off the screen can create a mismatch or an open pull-up.

howTo.detail: Start your cut at full speed, 2–3 steps before the screen. Set up your defender by leaning one way, then explode off the screener's shoulder.
howTo.title: Set up and sprint into the screen

howTo.detail: Your path should nearly touch the screener. A tight curl keeps the trailing defender stuck behind the screen.
howTo.title: Stay shoulder-tight to the screener

howTo.detail: Glance over your inside shoulder as you come off. If the defender trails, keep running to space; if he goes under, you are open; if they switch, attack the mismatch.
howTo.title: Read the defender mid-cut

howTo.detail: Catch with your feet already in a shot-ready hop. The best screen shooters are balanced before the ball arrives.
howTo.title: Catch in a ready stance

howTo.detail: Shoot, drive the closeout, or relocate — the read you made mid-cut decides. Never catch and freeze.
howTo.title: Decide instantly: shoot or drive

title: Shooting Off Screens
whatIsIt: Shooting off screens means catching and scoring while coming off an off-ball screen — sprinting around a teammate's pick and shooting before the defense recovers. It is the signature skill of movement shooters: players who score without ever holding the ball for more than a second.

This is a full-body skill, not just a shot. The cut, the read of the defender, the footwork on the catch, and the release all happen in about two seconds. Done well, it produces the cleanest looks in basketball.
whyItMatters: Set defenses take away standing shots; movement creates new ones. Teams that can score off screens force defenses to chase, communicate, and switch — every one of which creates mistakes. For players, it is a superpower: you do not need the ball or elite athleticism to score 15 points, just elite movement and preparation.
